[SWS_CM_10411] Service method processing modes Upstream requirements: RS_CM_00211 ⌈ The following service method processing modes shall be supported: • Polling : Instead of calling a provided service method, the Communication Man- agement software collects incoming service method invocations. The processing of each invocation is explicitly triggered by the implementation providing the ser- vice method using the mechanism defined in [SWS_CM_00199]. • Event-driven, concurrent : The Communication Management software activates the invoked service method when the invocation arrives. Consumer concurrent calls are allowed and will be processed concurrently on provider side by using different threads. This is the default mode. • Event-driven, sequential : The Communication Management software activates the invoked service method when the invocation arrives. Consumer concurrent calls are allowed, but will not be processed concurrently on provider side, by instead executing them one after the other to avoid the need of synchronization mechanisms in the implementation providing the service method. ⌋ The ProcessNextMethodCall() defined in [SWS_CM_00199] allows the imple- mentation providing the service method to trigger the execution of the next service con- sumer method call at a specific point of time if the processing mode is set to Polling . 7.5.7 Registering handler with null pointer [SWS_CM_10417] Register handlers failure due to null pointer or empty function. Specification of Communication Management AUTOSAR AP R25-11 [SWS_CM_00140] Minimum Send Interval monitoring for transmission requests for Triggers ⌈ To protect receivers from flooding/overload, each trigger shall have a configurable Minimum Send Interval (see ServiceInterfaceDeploymentEle- ment . minimumSendInterval ), which specifies the minimum amount of time that shall pass between two consecutive transmissions, i.e., the Minimum Send Interval limits the maximum Tx frequency of a given trigger in the network. If the application requests transmission of a trigger by calling Trigger::Send()/Send() , ara::com shall check, whether the time since the last successful handover of the trigger to the underlying transmission layer is greater than the specified Minimum Send Interval, i.e., the Minimum Send Interval is not violated. If the trigger has never been sent before, this shall also successfully pass the Minimum Send Interval check. If the Minimum Send Interval is not violated, ara::com shall process the transmission request by handing over the trigger to the transmission layer. The time of handover shall count as start of the new Minimum Send Interval monitoring. If the Minimum Send Interval is vio- lated, ara::com shall discard the transmission request and return error ComErrc:: kMinimumSendIntervalViolationError (see [SWS_CM_10432]). If the config- ured Minimum Send Interval ( ServiceInterfaceDeploymentElement . minimum- SendInterval ) of a trigger has the value 0, the Minimum Send Interval monitoring shall not be active for the corresponding trigger. ⌋ [SWS_CM_00142] Default value of Minimum Send Interval and disabling Mini- mum Send Interval monitoring for Triggers ⌈ If the configured Minimum Send Inter- val ( ServiceInterfaceDeploymentElement . minimumSendInterval ) of a trig- ger has the value 0, the Minimum Send Interval monitoring shall not be active for the corresponding trigger, i.e., ara::com will not limit the Tx frequency by dropping trans- mission requests. For each Trigger of a ServiceInterfaceDeployment (or the associated Event), 0 shall be the default value for the corresponding ServiceInter- faceDeploymentElement . minimumSendInterval . This means that unless Ser- viceInterfaceDeploymentElement . minimumSendInterval for a given event is explicitly configured to be > 0, the Tx rate is not limited by ara::com . ⌋ 7.5.17 Service trigger subscription For the service trigger subscription C++ API reference, see chapter 8.3.7.1.3. Specification of Communication Management AUTOSAR AP R25-11 7.5.22.2 Event Related Data Types For the Event Related Data Types C++ API reference, see chapter 8.9.1, 8.5.1.6, 8.5.1.1 8.5.1.10 and 8.5.1.11. Event handling on receiver side is based on queued communication with config- urable cache sizes. The cache size for a specific event of a proxy instance is de- termined by the Communication Management, when subscribing to a specific event by [SWS_CM_00141]. After the receiver subscribed to an event, the method GetNewSamples , as defined in [SWS_CM_00701], is used to retrieve the data samples of that event. In the context of GetNewSamples application provided callback functions are called by the Communica- tion Management, where Sample Pointer s to the data samples retrieved from under- lying queues are passed in. A Sample Pointer (see [SWS_CM_00306]) is an alias for an event data type pointer. On the event provider side, it is possible to let the Communication Management allocate the memory for the storage of the data before sending it as defined in [SWS_CM_90438]. A ara::com::SampleAllocateePtr (see [SWS_CM_00308]) is an alias for an event data type pointer used both for allocation and data sending. The event receiver can register an Event Receive Handler (see [SWS_CM_00309]) as a callback to get notified if new event data has arrived. The callback function itself is defined in the event consumer implementation; the Event Receive Handler type is just an general purpose function alias for the use in the method SetReceiveHandler() as defined by [SWS_CM_00181]. The event receiver can monitor the state of a service event subscription by re- questing or getting a notification of the Subscription State (see [SWS_CM_00310], [SWS_CM_00316] and [SWS_CM_00311]), as the real process of subscription might happen at a later point in time than the return of the call to Subscribe . The Subscrip- tion State related ara::com API methods require the definitions of a Subscription State enumeration ([SWS_CM_00310]) and a Subscription State Changed Handler function wrapper. 7.5.22.3 Trigger Related Data Types For the Trigger Related Data Types C++ API reference, see chapter 8.5.1.12.
